item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"CIDE’s 2023–2024 institutional program received a positive CONAHCYT opinion, and the center described its mission as producing rigorous social-science knowledge, educating professionals and public servants, and informing public policy for Mexico’s social and economic development. The report also records research lines covering public administration, corruption, policy evaluation, transparency, public expenditure, violence, human rights, security, macroeconomics, inequality, and migration.","question_ids":["1B.7","1B.9","3B.4","3B.7","4B.6","5B.2","5B.7","6B.5","8B.1"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The program and research agenda were active during 2023; the document does not establish that López Obrador personally directed them.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect institutional context during López Obrador’s federal administration; CONAHCYT is the federal science council, but the report does not attribute the positive opinion or research agenda specifically to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source describes CIDE’s institutional purposes and fields, not federal implementation or ruler conduct.","No direct evidence is provided about nuclear risk, international peace, domestic-security outcomes, personal integrity, or the ruler’s compliance with oversight."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"CIDE reported a decline in total personnel from 460 in the first semester of 2021 and 425 in 2022 to 421 in the first semester of 2023; academic personnel fell from 219 in 2021 and 186 in 2022 to 172 in 2023. Its 112 titular researchers were 99% doctoral degree holders and 83% members of the national researchers’ system; nine personnel, including one researcher in the former CONAHCYT chair program, left during the period, while 12 titular researchers and several visiting or invited academics were hired.","question_ids":["1B.7","4B.4","4B.5","5B.2","6B.4","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The staffing figures and hiring/departure events cover January–June 2023, with comparisons to prior years.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies the former CONAHCYT chair program and the CIDE staffing environment during López Obrador’s administration but does not prove that the ruler caused the staffing changes or appointments.","limitations":["The report does not identify the reasons for most staffing changes or establish political interference, loyalty tests, or protection of dissent.","The figures exclude the internal control body, external professors, and externally funded project staff."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"During January–June 2023, CIDE recorded three approved evaluations of titular researchers and appointed directors of the Legal Studies, Development Studies, and Economics divisions for two-year terms; it also operated 14 active educational programs with 443 students and 146 courses taught by 110 internal and 43 external professors.","question_ids":["1B.7","4B.4","5B.2","6B.4","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These evaluations, appointments, programs, and teaching activities occurred in the first semester of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The appointments and evaluations are attributed to CIDE’s director and internal academic processes, not directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["This evidence concerns CIDE’s internal administration and does not show federal appointment quality or ruler control over institutions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"CIDE maintained an Office of Pedagogical Advice and Emotional Support, handled a gender-discrimination and gender-violence protocol case, provided individual support to 53 students, conducted group interventions addressing harassment and discrimination, and awarded 85 new socioeconomic maintenance scholarships from 88 applications; 190 undergraduate students held maintenance scholarships during the first semester.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The support, protocol activity, and scholarships were reported for spring or the first semester of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These were CIDE institutional actions; the report does not attribute them to López Obrador or establish federal funding causation.","limitations":["The source provides no national incidence or distributional comparison and does not show whether federal policy caused or constrained these services."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":20,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"CIDE reported 11 new projects in January–June 2023, including four externally funded research projects and seven continuing-education programs, with estimated values of approximately 958,139 pesos and 10.6 million pesos respectively. It reported 11.554 million pesos in external-project convention value for January–June 2023, after reporting zero for 2022, and stated that no new research projects were opened in the semester while existing work aimed to improve public-policy design and implementation.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The reported projects and funding cover January–June 2023; the comparison includes 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes CIDE’s externally funded activities and does not establish that López Obrador selected, funded, or evaluated them.","limitations":["Reported values are estimated or convention values, not evidence of executed federal expenditure or policy outcomes.","The source does not identify the share of funding originating from the federal government."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":39,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"CIDE stated that changes since 2021 prevented the administration of external research funds and that the Mexico Researchers program participants completed their commission at CIDE in the first semester of 2023; consequently, primary data collection for the PANEL poverty-research program was suspended indefinitely. The report also records that CIDE had delivered technical and financial reports for three CONAHCYT-funded projects in 2020 but was still awaiting formal closure from CONAHCYT, while another corruption-policy project remained in its final stage.","question_ids":["1B.7","4B.4","5B.2","5B.7","6B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The suspension and unresolved closures were reported as of January–June 2023, with some underlying administrative events dating to 2020–2021.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the funding-administration changes and conclusion of the researchers’ commissions to institutional changes at CIDE and CONAHCYT, institutions operating under López Obrador’s administration, but does not state that he personally ordered them.","limitations":["The source does not specify which decisions caused the inability to administer external funds or identify responsible officials.","The pending closures may reflect administrative delay rather than misuse or deliberate obstruction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":54,"end_unit":56,"fact_summary":"CIDE projects in 2023 addressed the economic and social effects of delivery platforms, development along the Maya Train route, Mexican public opinion and foreign policy, and evaluation of three programs of the State of Mexico judiciary. One project explicitly situates its survey in the context of the federal government headed by Andrés Manuel López Obrador and Morena’s legislative majority, while also identifying China’s rise, COVID-19, the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and vaccine rollout as relevant contextual changes.","question_ids":["2B.10","3B.4","4B.4","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The projects were initiated or active in January–June 2023, while some contextual changes span the preceding years.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly identifies López Obrador as head of the federal government and describes Morena’s legislative position, but it does not evaluate his decisions or attribute the projects’ findings to him.","limitations":["The project descriptions state objectives and planned deliverables, not completed outcomes or verified policy effects.","The judiciary evaluation concerns the State of Mexico, not the federal executive."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":57,"end_unit":58,"fact_summary":"CIDE maintained projects on competition policy, privacy and data governance, economic development in the southeast, open-government measurement, public-policy evaluation, government management, and professional training. The open-government project measured transparency and participation from governmental and citizen perspectives, including access to information, active transparency, and open data, with planned reports, open datasets, and visualization tools.","question_ids":["1B.9","4B.6","4B.9","5B.4","5B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These projects were listed as ongoing during January–June 2023, although several originated earlier.","ruler_attribution":"The source documents independent CIDE research and training rather than López Obrador’s own policy decisions; it provides context relevant to federal transparency, privacy, competition, and digital-risk governance.","limitations":["Project objectives and planned products do not prove that the federal government adopted or implemented the recommendations.","No direct evidence is supplied about the ruler’s personal support for or obstruction of these safeguards."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":68,"end_unit":68,"fact_summary":"CIDE reported a project to operate and update the Angelus system for the National Search Commission, using document digitization, image processing, and natural-language techniques to analyze approximately six million pages concerning serious human-rights violations and disappearances; intended outputs included systems, methodologies, expert training, and reports to support families’ right to truth.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.1","3B.4","3B.10","6B.5","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The project was listed as ongoing in the 2023 report, with the underlying documentary material covering decades of state operations.","ruler_attribution":"The project involved the National Search Commission during López Obrador’s administration, but the report does not establish personal direction, funding decisions, or completed results by López Obrador.","limitations":["The source describes intended technical outputs and the historical scope of the records, not completed recovery, accountability, or victim remedy.","It does not determine whether the disappearances were caused by current federal authorities."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":82,"end_unit":90,"fact_summary":"CIDE researchers maintained regular public-facing media work during the first semester of 2023 on issues including the INAI, electoral reform and Plan B, the Supreme Court, the Guardia Nacional, militarization, violence, corruption, the president and the armed forces, and the prospective succession. The report records 154 total radio and television participations by academic personnel and 12 titular researchers with regular press collaborations.","question_ids":["2B.6","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","6B.5","7B.1","7B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The media appearances and listed articles cover January–June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report shows that critical and analytical public discussion of López Obrador’s government occurred through CIDE researchers and independent media outlets; it does not establish whether López Obrador personally permitted, pressured, or retaliated against them.","limitations":["Article titles and participation counts do not establish the factual accuracy of the commentary or official responses.","The source does not document censorship, retaliation, correction, or legal outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f6edcd346f522729","start_unit":114,"end_unit":123,"fact_summary":"CIDE organized open and closed events in 2023 involving electoral reform, AI for research, data protection, migration and refugee rights, gender violence, militarization, drug policy, public-policy evaluation, transparency, communication, and social policy. Several events included external universities, public agencies, civil-society organizations, journalists, and officials, including INE, CONEVAL, INEGI, INAES, and an adviser to the President of the Republic.","question_ids":["1B.7","1B.9","3B.4","3B.7","4B.3","4B.6","5B.7","6B.5","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The events occurred between January and June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The events demonstrate plural academic and policy engagement during López Obrador’s administration; the report does not show that López Obrador attended, directed, funded, or acted on their content.","limitations":["Event organization and participation do not prove policy adoption, implementation, or independent institutional protection.","The presence of an adviser to the President at one event does not establish presidential approval of the event’s views or recommendations."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["This document is an institutional self-evaluation by CIDE, not a direct assessment of Andrés Manuel López Obrador.","Most evidence concerns CIDE’s activities, staffing, research, and public events; direct evidence about the ruler’s conduct is limited.","The document covers January–June 2023 rather than the full calendar year, and several projects report objectives or planned deliverables rather than verified outcomes."]}
